messages:
support_alex: FYI escalation from CS — customer reports a bunch of streaming responses being counted as 5xx. They see client sockets close immediately after last chunk and we bill as 5xx. sample ids: req_9c12, req_9c13, timestamp ~2026-03-16T23:45Z. They provided curl repro and a pcap.
support_alex: Repro steps they gave: `curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer <key>\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream -d '{\"prompt\":\"hi\"}'` -> server sends chunks then client FIN, but metrics show 502/5xx. Customer angry about chargeback risk. cc @eng_oncall_ben @sre_maya
eng_oncall_ben: pinging in. Do we have gateway logs for those request ids? can we tie to an upstream error or proxy-level ECONNRESET vs server 5xx?
ops-bot: deploybot: streaming-runtime v2.14 deployed at 2026-03-16T22:58:03Z to canaries
sre_maya: I pulled gateway/nginx logs: for req_9c12 I see `upstream prematurely closed connection` and `client: 10.2.3.45, server: api, request: \"POST /v1/stream\"`, upstream_status empty, then `recv() failed (104: Connection reset by peer)`. That looks like client-initiated close, but our metrics pipeline currently classifies these as 5xx when upstream doesn't report 2xx. Need to confirm raw tcp traces.
support_alex: Attached the customer's pcap extract. They show server wrote final chunk and then immediately FIN from client. server socket shows `write: 200 OK chunks`, then `send -> FIN`, then gateway logs `upstream closed` and we mark 502.
eng_runtime_lead: Noted. We shipped a small change in chunked trailer handling in v2.14 to aggressively flush trailers. If the trailer flush syscall errors (EPIPE) after we wrote body, the runtime surfaces an upstream error to gateway. That could explain misclassification: server produced body but trailing flush failed and runtime bubbled an error so gateway sees non-2xx. Commit: cf3a9e2. Reverting that part is possible.
eng_oncall_ben: Can we reproduce locally with a quick client that closes right after last byte? I'll try a tiny script to connect, read first few chunks then close without reading trailers.
sre_maya: Quick mitigation suggestion: change the metrics classification rule to treat `recv() failed (104)` or `ECONNRESET` with elapsed_time < 2s after last write as client-abort (not 5xx). We can hotpatch that rule in infra for the next 24h while eng patches runtime.
support_alex: Customer-success_anna asked for ETA to stop the billing hits. CS wants wording to tell customer. Anna: \"we can temporarily exclude these from 5xx billing while we fix, ETA 6-12 hours?\"
eng_runtime_lead: I'll cut a patch to stop treating trailer flush EPIPE as server failure and instead return success if body was sent. If QA passes, can ship to canary in ~3h, full rollout ~8h. Will open PR and link.
eng_oncall_ben: Reprobed locally: simple Python client that closes right after reading final chunk triggers exactly the same gateway log sequence. I filed a quick-runbook: `if gateway log shows recv() failed + no upstream_status and app log shows trailer_flush error -> classify as client-abort`. I'll push the hotpatch rule now.
support_alex: I'll tell CS: temporary exclusion enabled, engineering patch in progress, we will follow up with root-cause and a compensating assessment for affected billing window. :thumbsup:
customer-success-anna: copying customer note they asked us to preserve request ids for audit: req_9c12 req_9c13. Also they want postmortem when fixed.
eng_runtime_lead: PR opened: https://git.redwood/infra/runtime/pull/342 — patch changes trailer flush error handling and adds a defensive metric tag `stream_trailer_failure=client_abort_candidate`. QA run in progress.
ops-bot: alert: hotpatch rule applied to metrics classifier at 2026-03-17T01:02:10Z (rule id: svc-metrics-guard-71)
sre_maya: After hotpatch, historical reaggregation of last hour shows 64% drop in 5xx count for streaming route. Will monitor for false negatives.
support_alex: Thanks team. I'll mark this as escalation-resolved-for-now and will reopen if customer sees more.
